This report compares seven forecasting models for U.S. CPI inflation, following Faust and Wright (2013), in an expanding-window experiment with forecast origins from 1999Q4 and targets through 2019Q4.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(fpp3)          # tsibble, feasts, dplyr, tidyr, ggplot2
library(readr)
library(slider)
library(patchwork)
library(urca)          # ADF and KPSS tests (Step 1)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 9))

source("R/01_data.R")
source("R/02_harness.R")
source("R/models_benchmarks.R")
source("R/models_ar_gap.R")
source("R/models_direct.R")
source("R/03_evaluate.R")
source("R/04_diagnostics.R")

q <- load_quarterly()      # quarterly data, 1960Q1 onward, built from data/
```

# Data

The data are the course repository's monthly FRED series for headline CPI (`CPIAUCSL`), the unemployment rate (`UNRATE`), and the three-month Treasury bill rate (`TB3MS`), unchanged from Stage 1. Each quarter takes its quarter-end month, inflation is $\pi_t=400\log(P_t/P_{t-1})$, and December 1959 CPI is the base for 1960Q1. `R/01_data.R` builds the series and checks it against Stage 1 (160 estimation quarters, 1960Q1 inflation of zero, and a 1960Q2 hand calculation).

```{r}
#| label: data-summary
q |> as_tibble() |> group_by(period) |>
  summarize(start = format(min(qtr)), end = format(max(qtr)), quarters = n())
```

# Step 2: Expanding-window forecast experiment

A forecast origin $T$ is the quarter in which a forecast is made and the last quarter in the estimation sample. The first origin is 1999Q4. At each origin, the harness passes every model only the quarters from 1960Q1 through $T$. Each model builds any one-sided variables, selects lags, estimates, and forecasts from that sample alone, and the $h=1$, 4, and 8 forecasts are saved with their origin and target quarter. The origin then moves forward one quarter and the process repeats, so the estimation sample grows by one quarter each time.

Realized inflation for the target quarter is attached only after a forecast is saved, and the error is $e^{(h)}_{j,t}=\pi_t-\widehat\pi^{(h)}_{j,t\mid t-h}$, so a positive error means the model underpredicted. Because 2019Q4 is the last target, longer horizons have fewer errors. The harness confirms the counts and target ranges match the design: 80 errors at $h=1$ (origins 1999Q4 to 2019Q3), 77 at $h=4$, and 73 at $h=8$. Model specifications, including variables, lag ranges, and estimation methods, are fixed before any errors are examined.

```{r}
#| label: harness
models <- list(
  "Random walk"    = model_rw,
  "4Q average"     = model_4q,
  "AR(p)"          = model_ar,
  "Direct AR"      = model_direct_ar,
  "Gap AR"         = model_gap_ar,
  "Fixed gap"      = model_gap_fixed,
  "Phillips curve" = model_phillips
)
models <- available_models(models, q)     # skips any model still marked TODO
if (length(models) > 0) {
  results <- run_harness(q, models)
  write_csv(results |> mutate(across(c(origin, target), format)), "results/forecasts.csv")
  check_error_counts(results) |> distinct(h, n, first_target, last_target)
}
```

)

diag$ljung_box
diag$by_decade
diag$largest
